record.original_question: For every geometrically finite rational map f, is every connected component of its Julia set locally connected?

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Show every component of J is locally connected.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ be a rational map of degree at least $2$ acting on the Riemann sphere. Denote by $J(f)$ its Julia set and by $F(f)$ its Fatou set. Recall that $f$ is called geometrically finite if every critical point of $f$ that lies in the Julia set has a finite forward orbit (equivalently, every critical point is either preperiodic or its forward orbit is contained in the union of basins of attracting and parabolic periodic cycles).

Prove or disprove: for every geometrically finite rational map $f$, every connected component of the Julia set $J(f)$ is locally connected.
artifact.status_search_result: The local connectivity of every connected component of the Julia set of a geometrically finite rational map was established by Tan Lei and Yin Yongcheng. Their work, building on earlier results for hyperbolic and subhyperbolic maps, proves local connectivity by constructing expanding conformal metrics in neighborhoods of Julia components. The result is now standard in complex dynamics.

status_evidence.title: On local connectivity for the Julia set of rational maps
status_evidence.snippet: Local connectivity for Julia sets of rational maps, including the geometrically finite case.
status_evidence.claim: Local connectivity for Julia components of geometrically finite rational maps is established in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Local connectivity of Julia sets of some rational maps with Siegel disks
status_evidence.snippet: By constructing expanding metrics, the connected Julia sets of hyperbolic, subhyperbolic and geometrically finite rational maps have been proved to be locally connected.
status_evidence.claim: Connected Julia sets of geometrically finite rational maps are known to be locally connected (Tan-Yin).
